 JUDGMENT

The Petitioners have filed these petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicle Act seeking compensation for the death and injury sustained by Sri.Basavaraju A. and Sri.Ramesh respectively,
in a road accident dated 06.05.2018.
Both the petitions arisen out of a common accident.

Therefore,
both the petitions are clubbed together as per order dated 25.02.2020 and common evidence is recorded and common judgment is passed.

2. The case of the Petitioners is as under:
On 06.05.2018 at about 8.30pm Mr.Basavaraju A. (deceased) and Mr.Ramesh were proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA42R5745 as a rider and pillion rider to go to Chikkadevarahalli to Harohalli, when they reached near Anjaneya Temple, near Thamasandra, NH209, Bangalore SCCH-25 Road, Ramangara Dist, at that time one Ashoka Leyland Ape bearing No.KA53B9392 came with high speed,
driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life and dashed to the motorcycle, due to impact both were fell down and sustained injuries.
3.

The Petitioners in MVC No.5712/2018 stated that, immediately after the accident Basavaraju was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Harohalli, took first aid then shifted to Pinacle Hospital, Mysore Road,
Bangalore, the doctor operated the spine and head injury, but on 29.06.2018 he was died.
So far they have spent Rs.15,00,000/ towards treatment, conveyance, food and nourishment, funeral and other expenses.

Before the accident the deceased Basavaraju was working as a Driver in the Garments and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month, he was very much helpful to his family in all the aspects and he having wife and two children SCCH-25 and aged mother and he was the only earning member in the family.

After the death of Basavaraju the entire family is suffering the food,
cloth and education maintenance.

4. It is further case of the Petitioner in MVC 5284/2018 that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Harohalli, took first aid then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Bangalore, the doctor operated the right leg and inserted the rod and screws, underwent several medical, clinical radiological examinations, laboratory tests, X rays were taken he treated for the injuries sustained and doctor advised for a bed rest with regular follow up treatment up to one year.
So far he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards treatment, conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses.

The doctor advised for one more operation of removal of implants, he is still suffering from pain in the right leg, he is in deep mental agony, he cannot do his SCCH-25 work as he was doing earlier and he cannot do his regular activities, he cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.

He was physically strong hale and healthy before the accident Nos.2 And 3 Are vs Is The Insurer Of The Offending Vehicle ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172955215/
3 and was working as a Lorry Driver and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.

Due to this accident, he has lost the income and future prospective life, happiness, earning capacity and has become disabled and dependent and suffering a lot mentally, physically and financially and now he cannot discharge his duty effectively due to the disability and pain.

5. The petitioners have further submitted that, the Harohalli Police have registered a Criminal case against the Driver of the TATA AC bearing No.KA53B9392 in Cr.No.153/2018 punishable u/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The said police have investigated the matter and filed a charge sheet against the Driver of the TATA ACE.
1 st respondent is SCCH-25 the RC owner, 2nd respondent is the Driver and the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to them.
6. In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.2 did not appear and hence, placed ex parte.
In response to the summons issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent Nos.1 and 3 appeared and filed separate written statements.

7. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement has denied the case of the petitioners as false and submitted that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of their vehicle but there was sole negligence on the part of the rider of the bike as the respondent No.2 was driving the vehicle very slowly by following the traffic rules and regulations on the left side of the road, came near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, at Thamasandra NH209, Bangalore Road, Harohalli, at that time the deceased SCCH-25 Basavaraju riding the bike in a rash and negligent manner without following the traffic rules and without observing the movements of the vehicles on the road and suddenly came to the opposite of his vehicle and caused the accident.

Further submitted that as on the date of accident the vehicle had valid insurance and hence he is not liable to pay any compensation and accordingly prayed for dismissal of the petitions against him.
8.

The Respondent No.3 in the written statement has denied the case of the petitioners as false,
admitted issuance of insurance policy but their liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and submitted that there is non compliance of Secs.134(C) and 158(6) of MV Act 1988.
Further submitted that, the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
The deceased himself was solely responsible for the alleged accident.
The deceased was not wearing helmet as SCCH-25 on the date of accident.
The driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective DL as on the date of accident being willfully entrusted by the respondent No.1 in contravention of the policy conditions.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petitions against them.

9. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues: In MVC.5712/2018 1 Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Basavaraju A.?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Ashoka Leyland Ape bearing Reg.No.KA53B9392 as a result Basavaraju A.
sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries?

10. The Petitioners in MVC No.5712/2018 in order to prove their case they have examined Smt.Shobha K. - Wife of Late Basavaraju A. as PW.1 and produced 17 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.17.

They have also examined Mr.Sampath B. Shetty - Medical Record Keeper at Pinacle Hospital,
Byatarayanapura, Mysore Road, Bangalore, as PW.4 and produced 3 documents as per Exs.P.25 to P.27.
The Petitioner in MVC No.5284/2018 has got examined himself as PW.2 and produced 6 documents as Exs.P.18 to P.22 & P.28.

He has SCCH-25 also examined Dr.S.Ramachandra - Asst.
Professor of Orthopedic at Victoria Hospital as PW.3 and produced 2 documents as per Exs.P.23 and P.24.
On the other side the Respondent No.3 has examined Mr.Mahesh Prasad - Dy.Manager as RW.1 and produced 1 document as per Ex.R.1.

It has also examined Mr.Nityananda S.  SDA, KR Pura RTO, Bangalore, as RW.2 and produced 1 document as per Ex.R.2 and Mr.Prakash R.  Dy.SP,
ACB, Bangalore City, examined as RW.3 and produced 3 documents as per Exs.R.3 to R.5.
11.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials on record.

PWs.1 and 2 have specifically deposed in their chief examination that the driver of the offending SCCH-25 Leyland Ape bearing Reg. No.KA53B9392 driven it at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to Nos.2 And 3 Are vs Is The Insurer Of The Offending Vehicle ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172955215/
5 human life and dashed to the motorcycle in which the deceased and the petitioner were proceeding as a rider and pillion rider and caused the accident.

On the other side, the Respondent Nos.1 and 3 have denied that the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident occurred solely due to negligence of the deceased.

In the cross examination of PW.1 it is elicited that due to head on collusion the accident took place, the front side of bike completely got damaged, similarly the front right side of the offending vehicle got damaged, the deceased and the petitioner were not wearing helmet on the alleged dated of accident,
the deceased was not holding valid DL.
14.
In the crossexamination of PW.2, he clearly admitted that there was a head on collusion between the SCCH-25 vehicles, front side of both vehicles got damaged, deceased sustained head injury.

15. In support of the defence the respondent No.3 has got examined its official as RW.1 who deposed that there was complete negligence on the part of deceased and there was breach of policy conditions.
In the crossexamination it is elicited that the charge sheet is filed against their insured vehicle.

16. By relying on the police documents the counsel for the respondent No.3 contends that there was negligence on the part of the deceased and therefore the documents needs to be appreciated in this aspect and the RW.1's evidence is only formal in nature with regard to alleged manner of accident as he had not witnessed the accident and admittedly the charge sheet is filed against the offending vehicle only.
On perusal of Ex.P.2 the accident occurred at 8.30pm on 06.05.2018 when SCCH-25 the offending vehicle dashed to the right side of the bike.

On perusal of Exs.P.4 and P.5 it reveals that the accident spot is on the left side of the two way road i.e., on the lane in which the bike was proceeding and further makes it clear that the offending vehicle deviated from its lane and came to the opposite side of the lane in which the bike was coming and hence there is no any contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and hence the contention raised by the counsel for the respondent No.3 is not acceptable and their defence in this regard remained unproved.

17. Further, the FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, inquest report, PM report, IMV report and charge sheet produced by the Petitioners as per Exs.P.1 to P.9 are the public documents which are issued by a public office and they have got presumptive value under law.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and SCCH-25 documents produced by them.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PWs.1 and 2 coupled with documents produced by them this court is of the opinion that, the driver of the offending Ashok Leyland Ape bearing Reg.No.KA53B9392 had driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident, result of which petitioner Ramesh and Basavaraj A. have sustained grievous injuries and Basavaraj A. succumbed to the injuries during the treatment.

Accordingly Issue No.2 in MVC No.
5712/2018 and Issue No.1 in MVC No.5284/2018 are held in the affirmative.

6 It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the minor children and the petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased - Basavaraj A.
The Petitioners to prove this relationship have examined the SCCH-25 first Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically deposed this relationship in her chief examination.
Apart from that to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have also produced Voter's ID and Adhar Cards of the Petitioners and the deceased as per Exs.P.13 to P.17.
In Ex.P.16 - Voter's ID Card of the deceased, his father's name is mentioned as Late Appajaiah.
Ex. P.14
- Aadhar Card of the Petitioner No.1 who is the wife of the deceased, her husband's name is mentioned as Basavaraju A..
Ex. P.15
- Aadhar Card of the Petitioner No.4 who is the mother of the deceased, her husband's name is mentioned as Appajaiah who is the father of the deceased.
In Exs.P.13 and P.17 - Aadhar cards of the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 their father's name is mentioned as Basavaraju.
It is pertinent to note that Exs
to P.17 are public documents which have got presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents in the cross examination.
The Respondent No.3 SCCH-25
have not produced any contrary documents.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and Exs.P.13 to P.17 this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and the Petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the minor children and Petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased - Basavaraju A..
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3 in MVC 5712/2018:

The PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased - Basavaraju A., they have lost the bread earner of their family and their loving husband, father and Son.
They have pleaded that they have spent more than Rs.15,00,000/ towards medical treatment, conveyance, food and nourishment charges, funeral and other incidental expenses.
They have also examined Mr.Sampath SCCH-25 B.Shetty as PW.4 and produced 3 documents as per Exs.P.25 to P.27.
In the crossexamination of PW.4 nothing worth is elicited.
From this document it is clear that the deceased took treatment in the said hospital.
This court while discussing the Issue No.2 has come to the conclusion that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending Ashok Leyland Ape Lorry.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation.

Monthly income:
20.
According to the Petitioners the deceased was hale and heath and he was doing Driver work and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
But, in this regard, the Petitioners have not produced any documents such as bank statement, vouchers etc..
In the absence of specific documents for proof of income, the version of the Petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/ per month is not acceptable.
Under such SCCH-25 circumstances, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.
At the time of accident the deceased was a young aged person.
The accident took place in the year 2018.

Therefore, having regard to the age of Nos.2 And 3 Are vs Is The Insurer Of The Offending Vehicle ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172955215/
7 the deceased and taking judicial notice of the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.12,500/
per month.

As such, Petitioners are entitled for the following compensation: Age of the deceased:
21.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced Notarized copy of Election ID of the deceased as per Ex.P.16.
As per Ex.P.16, his date of birth is 01.06.1991, the accident was occurred in the year 2018.
As such, as on the date of accident the deceased was 27 years.
The Respondent No.3 have not placed any contrary SCCH-25 documents.
Therefore, relying upon the said Voter's ID Card/Ex.P.16, his age is considered as 27 years.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has wife, two minor children and mother that is petitioners 1 to 4.
In the cross examination of PW.1 she stated that her motherinlaw is staying in her brotherin law's house.
From this it is clear that the petitioner No.4 is not residing with the petitioners and appears to be looked after by her another son.
Therefore, the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are only considered as dependents.

It is relevant to note that as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in special leave petition No. 25590/2014 between National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others and other SCCH-25 connected petitions, even in case of the self employed and fixed salary also future prospects needs to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others and other SCCH-25 connected
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, in the present case since the deceased is below 40 years age group, 40% future prospects have to be added to his monthly income.
As per the Sarala Verma case, as the deceased has only three dependents and hence 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

If 40% income is added to his monthly income,
it comes around Rs.17,500/ (Rs.12,500/ + Rs.5,000/) and 1/3rd of his income is deducted towards his living and personal expenses, balance comes to Rs.11,667/ (Rs.17,500/  Rs.5,833/).

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.23,80,068/ (Rs.11,667/ X 12 X 17 =
Rs.23,80,068/).
SCCH-25 ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
She has lost her husband at the age of 26 years and she has to live remaining part of her life without him.

Therefore,
she is entitled for compensation under the head of consortium.
In Magma General Insurance company Limited the Hon'ble Apex court has considered the compensation under head of loss of consortium.

The Hon'ble Apex court in three judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.

entities.text:
United Indian Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Paragraph 53 to 65, dealt with three conventional heads and discussed about "Consortium" to be a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, SCCH-25 which is a loss to his family.
Filial Consortium - A child's society, affection and companionship given to a parent.
Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for compensation under the head of consortium.

As such, the Petitioners are entitled a sum of Rs.1,60,000/ (Rs.40,000/
each) under this head.

8 iii) TRANSPORTATION, MEDICAL AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:

In so far as the funeral and transportation and medical expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have pleaded that they have spent more than Rs.15,00,000/ amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral obsequies and medical expenses.
In this regard they have produced 161 medical bills for a sum of Rs.7,23,369/ as per Ex.P.12 and also produced final bills issued by Pinnacle Hospital for a sum of Rs.6,32,000/ as per Ex.P.28.
In total the petitioners have SCCH-25 produced bills for a sum of Rs.13,55,369/.
There is no contrary to this documents from the respondents.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for the said amount under the heads of Medical Expenses.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the expenses for funeral and transportation of dead body.
However, looking into the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.20,000/ towards funeral and transportation expenses.
iv) LOSS TO THE ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was getting monthly income by doing Driver work and earning.
Out of this, he was getting 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the SCCH-25 Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss to the estate.
The total compensation comes to Rs.39,38,437/ and if it is rounded off it comes to Rs.39,38,500/
and as such in total the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.39,38,500/ and same is awarded under above different heads.
22. Issue No.2 in MVC No.5284/2018
: It is the further case of the Petitioner - Mr.Ramesh that, due to the accident, he has sustained injury to his head, right leg and on all over the body.

He took first aid treatment at Govt. Hospital, Haroahalli and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore,
operated to his right leg and inserted the rod and screws, underwent several medical, clinical,
radiological examination, laboratory tests Xrays were taken, he treated for the injuries sustained and advised him for bed rest with regular follow up treatment up to one year.

Due to SCCH-25 accidental injuries he cannot do his work as he was doing earlier and cannot do his regular activities and normal work, still suffering from pain in the right leg, he is in deep mental agony and lost his income and future prospective life, happiness, earning capacity and become disable and dependent.
In this regard, the Petitioner apart from examining himself as PW.2 has also examined Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW.3.
PW.3 has deposed supporting the version of the Petitioner.
This court while considering issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Ashok Leyland Ape.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Quantum of Disability:
23.
PW.3 -

sentences.text: PW.3 further deposed that, recently he has examined the petitioner exclusively for disability assessment, on clinical examination he found disabilities and on radiological examination revealed the following TYPE II Open fracture of left tibia shows UNION with implants failure proximal end of Nail along with 2 inter locking bolts are placed anterior to the bone.

PW.3 further deposed that the petitioner suffers the permanent residual physical disability of about 33.09% of left lower limb which is about 16.5% of whole body and the petitioner is advised to undergo SCCH-25 another operation for removal of implants form left Tibia.
However, it is relevant to note that this witness has not deposed anything about the functional disability of the Petitioner having reference to the nature of his work.
He has not stated how it would effect the profession or occupation of the Petitioner.

In the crossexamination PW.3 it is elicited that he has not consulted the treated doctor, fracture is united, the petitioner had only tibia fracture, in their hospital the implant removal surgery may cost within Rs.10,000/ and he has not advised any medication to the petitioner.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and the treatment taken and the age of the petitioner whole body disability assessed by the PW.3 appears to be on higher side.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by him, the period of treatment that he has undergone and his age

,
disability is considered as 8% to the whole body.

SCCH-25 Monthly income:
24.
According to the Petitioner, he was working as a Lorry Driver and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
But the Petitioner to prove his income has not produced any document such as bank extract, or voucher.
Therefore, version of the Petitioner that he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month is not acceptable.
At the time of accident the petitioner was 39 years old as per Aadhar Card/Ex.P.22.

Though the PW.2 in his cross examination admitted that he was aged more than 41 years at the time of accident but in support of the said admission there is no any documents produced and more over the Ex.P.22 issued in the year 2013 and hence the said document is considered to ascertain the age of the petitioner.
The accident took place in the year 2018.

Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased and relying the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda & Anr., in MFA SCCH-25 No:202534/2019(MVC) the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.12,500/ per month.
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:
As per the wound certificate - Ex.P.18 and the discharge summary - Ex.P.19, the Petitioner has sustained Rt. Leg - Swelling, tenderness, movements restricted.
Xray C/o isolated fracture Tibia (R) which is grievous in nature.
He took first aid treatment at Govt.
Hospital, Harohalli

and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore, admitted as an inpatient from 06.05.2018 to 29.05.2018 for 24 days and doctor operated the right leg and inserted the rod and screws, underwent several medical, clinical, radiological examinations, laboratory tests Xrays were taken he treated for the injuries SCCH-25 sustained and finally doctor advised for bed rest with regular follow up treatment.
Considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment that he has underwent, a sum of Rs.45,000/ is awarded under this head.

10 ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner stated that, he has spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
In this regard he has produced 28 medical bills for a sum of Rs.27,688/.
There is nothing contrary elicited in the cross examination about the medical bills.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for reimbursement of the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
In the absence of proof of income, the income of the Petitioner is considered as Rs.12,500/ per month.
As mentioned above he has sustained grievous injuries.
He took SCCH-25 treatment in the said above hospital for about 24 days as an inpatient and thereafter till today he is under treatment as an outpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner required one month time for recovering from the grievous injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled for a sum of Rs.12,500/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
In so far as age of the Petitioner is concerned, the Petitioner has produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.22.
As per this document his date of birth is 01.01.1979 and the accident was occurred on 06.05.2018.
As such he was 39 years as on the date of accident.
The Respondents have not placed any contrary documents.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is considered as 39 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to SCCH-25 his age is 15.

LIABILITY 26.

The Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the offending vehicle contended that as on the date of accident the driver of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL SCCH-25 to drive the said category of vehicle which is in contravention of policy conditions and hence they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In support of said defence the respondent no.3 has examined the RW.1 who has produced copy of policy.
In the cross examination to the RW.1 noting worth is elicited to disprove their said defence.

But however the petitioner is not competent to prove either the existence of valid DL or not as it is the duty of insured to prove the same but in this case the insured/R1 remained absent and hence the defence of the respondent No.3/Insurance Company is proved.
Further the insurance company has examined the RTO as RW.2 but he has stated that they are unable to trace out the DL particulars without any proper details.

Further examined the IO as RW.3 who has clearly deposed that as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle/accused had no valid and effective DL and the RW.3 has produced the true copies of police notice, reply to it and SCCH-25 copy of another police notice and clearly deposed that after thorough investigation he filed charge sheet by including relevant section for not holding DL.

27. The respondent No.3 further contends that as there is a breach of policy conditions and hence they are not liable to pay compensation and pay and recovery principles are also SCCH-25 not applicable to the case on hand.

On the other side the counsel for the petitioner submits that as the petitioner is third party and as the third party risk is covered under Ex.R.1 policy and hence if this Tribunal comes to conclusion that there is a breach of policy conditions then the pay and recovery needs to be ordered.

she is entitled for compensation under the head of consortium.
